name: @lenne.tech/cli
author: Kai Haase

scripts.check:fix: npm install && npm audit fix && npm run format && npm run lint:fix && npm run build && npm run check:start
scripts.build: npm run lint && npm run test && npm run clean-build && npm run compile && npm run copy-templates
scripts.copy-templates: npx shx cp -R ./src/templates ./build/templates && npx shx cp -R ./src/config ./build/config
scripts.reinit: npx rimraf package-lock.json && npx rimraf node_modules && npm i && npm run build

//devDependencies.@emnapi/core: Not imported by this CLI. @napi-rs/wasm-runtime 1.x moved @emnapi/core and @emnapi/runtime from dependencies to peerDependencies (napi-rs#3174), and the only path to them here is dev-only AND optional: eslint-plugin-import-x / jest-resolve > unrs-resolver > @unrs/resolver-binding-wasm32-wasi (cpu: wasm32) > @napi-rs/wasm-runtime. npm >= 11.5.0 (arborist 9.1.3) prunes nodes that are both peer and optional from the ideal tree, so it never writes them to the lockfile — while npm <= 11.4 still demands them and fails npm ci with "Missing: @emnapi/core@1.11.3 from lock file". Declaring them here is the remedy arborist's own source comment names: an optional peer stops being optional once a root dependency requires it, so both npm generations then agree. Verified: npm ci passes on npm 10 and 11.6, and npm install no longer strips the entries. Remove once @napi-rs/wasm-runtime declares them in peerDependenciesMeta as optional, or once npm >= 11.5 is the floor everywhere (GitHub Actions still runs Node 20 = npm 10).

//overrides.semver@*: Force latest semver 7.x across all sub-deps; gluegun@5.2.2 pins semver@7.7.0 which is stale - remove once gluegun updates its dep.
//overrides.brace-expansion@<1.1.21: Five DoS advisories, all patched in the 1.x line by 1.1.21: exponential-time expansion of consecutive non-expanding {} groups (GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp, high, fixed 1.1.16), unbounded expansion length causing an OOM crash (GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg, high, fixed 1.1.17), uncontrolled recursion in parseCommaParts (GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p, high, fixed 1.1.19), uncontrolled recursion on nested brace groups (GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7, high, fixed 1.1.20) and quadratic-time `{a},b}` rewrite (GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr, medium, fixed 1.1.21). Raised from 1.1.18 on 2026-10-03: 1.1.18 was still open to the last three. Transitive via dotgitignore/eslint/fs-jetpack/glob/test-exclude/ts-morph > minimatch. Latent today: the minimatch raises below leave no 1.x install in the tree (only brace-expansion 5.0.12), so this key catches a future minimatch 3.x consumer. One bounded key per affected major so each can only raise a vulnerable version, never cap a patched one - remove once minimatch requests the patched ranges.
//overrides.brace-expansion@>=2.0.0 <2.1.7: Same five advisories, 2.x line (fixed 2.1.2 / 2.1.3 / 2.1.5 / 2.1.6 / 2.1.7). Raised from 2.1.4 on 2026-10-03. Latent today, like the 1.x key.
//overrides.brace-expansion@>=5.0.0 <5.0.12: Same advisories, 5.x line, plus three newer DoS advisories fixed only in 5.0.10-5.0.12 (GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p, GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7, GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr; all high). Reaches production via gluegun > fs-jetpack > minimatch. Floored at >=5.0.0 so a future 3.x/4.x dependency is not silently forced across two majors.
//overrides.//minimatch-note: Why the minimatch raises exist: when they were added, brace-expansion 1.x and 2.x were END OF LINE for GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (advisory range <=5.0.7 across ALL majors, patched only 5.0.8+), so the only fix was to raise each CONSUMER off minimatch 3.x/5.x/9.x. That premise no longer holds: upstream has since backported every fix (GHSA-mh99 now reads <1.1.17 / >=2.0.0 <2.1.3, and 1.1.21 / 2.1.7 patch all five current advisories). Verified 2026-10-03 with fresh lockfile resolves: without `minimatch@>=4 <10` and `fs-jetpack > minimatch@<10` npm audit is still clean, the tree only gains minimatch 3.1.5 + 5.1.9 and brace-expansion 1.1.21 + 2.1.7 (7 packages). So both are now a DEDUPE measure (one minimatch 10.2.6, one brace-expansion 5.0.12), not a security fix - dropping them is a judgment call, it reopens no advisory. Forcing brace-expansion 5.x globally is still NOT an option: 5.x is ESM/tshy and exports an object ({ expand, ... }) while 1.x/2.x export the function itself, so minimatch 3.x/5.x would die on `expand is not a function`. Each scoped entry was verified against the consumer's actual call site before being added. The eslint / @eslint/eslintrc / @eslint/config-array entries were REMOVED in 1.42.0: eslint 10 requests minimatch ^10.2.5 itself, config-array ^10.2.4, and eslintrc is no longer in the tree at all.
//overrides.minimatch@>=4 <10: Bounded raise of every minimatch 4.x-9.x install to 10.2.6, whose brace-expansion ^5.0.8 is patched. As of 2026-10-03 the only consumer it still raises is filelist (gluegun > ejs 3.1.10 > jake > filelist, PRODUCTION-reachable, minimatch ^5.0.1): @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree 8.65 requests ^10.2.2 itself and the jest 30.5 packages no longer depend on minimatch. Verified safe: filelist calls only the static helper `minimatch.match(files, pat, opts)`. Floored at >=4 so the 3.x line is NOT swept in: minimatch 3.x is callable while 9.x/10.x export an object with __esModule but no `default` key, so sweeping it would break any consumer that calls the default export. Dedupe, not security (see //minimatch-note). Drop once filelist requests minimatch >=10.
//overrides.babel-plugin-istanbul > test-exclude@<8: Dedupe override, no longer a security fix. Added when babel-plugin-istanbul requested test-exclude ^6.0.0, whose 6.0.0 pins minimatch ^3.0.4 and glob ^7. Since jest 30.5 (babel-plugin-istanbul 8.0.0) the request is ^7.0.1, and test-exclude 7.0.2 already uses minimatch ^10.2.2: a fresh resolve without this entry audits clean (2026-10-03) but adds 23 packages (glob 10.5.0 and its subtree). 8.0.0 uses glob ^13, the major this project already ships, and is still CJS with the same `module.exports = TestExclude` class shape, so babel-plugin-istanbul 8's _interopRequireDefault + `new _testExclude.default(opts)` keeps working. Drop once babel-plugin-istanbul requests test-exclude ^8.
//overrides.fs-jetpack > minimatch@<10: Same chain, PRODUCTION-reachable (gluegun > fs-jetpack). Safe: lib/utils/matcher.js does `require('minimatch').Minimatch` and uses only `new Minimatch(pattern, { matchBase, nocomment, nocase, dot })`, `.negate` and `.match()` - all verified against 10.x. Not fixable by upgrading fs-jetpack: gluegun@5.2.2 is the latest release and fs-jetpack@5.1.0 still requests minimatch ^5.1.0 (brace-expansion ^2.0.1, also unpatched).

//jest.workerIdleMemoryLimit: Recycle a ts-jest worker once its heap passes this. Guards against an intermittent `A jest worker process was terminated by another process: signal=SIGSEGV` that kills ONE suite while every other test passes (seen twice in marketplace*, both under `npm run check`, never reproducible on demand - 0 in 9 targeted runs incl. --maxWorkers=16). It is a worker crash, NOT an assertion failure: the signature is `Test suite failed to run` with the remaining count still green. All versions are current and in-range (node 24 / jest 30 / ts-jest 29 / ts 6), so this is a resilience measure against unbounded worker heap growth, not a proven root-cause fix - if it recurs, capture the suite name and re-open.
